stem: Why can a root zone remain physiologically stressed even when water and mineral nutrients are abundant?
choices: Excess water can reduce gas-filled pore space and limit oxygen diffusion to roots
Wet media can slow nutrient diffusion enough to make mineral availability the primary stress mechanism
High water content can cool the substrate enough that temperature becomes the main limit on root metabolism
Frequent irrigation can dilute root-zone EC enough that osmotic stress becomes the dominant explanation
rationale: Roots require oxygen for respiration. When pores remain water-filled for too long, gas exchange and oxygen diffusion can become limiting even when water and nutrients are present.
